the soft, spiced contours of your flesh Invite me, and I come. I stay until dawn breathes its light and night slips away.
Leave Lebanon behind, and come. Leave your high mountain hideaway. Abandon your wilderness seclusion, Where you keep company with lions and panthers guard your safety.
You looked at me, and I fell in love. One look my way and I was hopelessly in love!
far more pleasing than a fine, rare wine, your fragrance more exotic than select spices.
every syllable you speak a delicacy to savor. Your clothes smell like the wild outdoors, the ozone scent of high mountains.
a whole orchard of succulent fruits— Ripe apricots and peaches, oranges and pears; Nut trees and cinnamon, and all scented woods;
fed by spring waters from the Lebanon mountains.
get moving, South Wind! Breathe on my garden, fill the air with spice fragrance. Oh, let my lover enter his garden! Yes, let him eat the fine, ripe fruits.
